body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR DIAGNOSIS IS CONFIRMED AND IT REACHES FURTHER THAN YOUR SEAT. Also: your correction about the #2040 damage crossed my mail and is already out of date - I recovered the prior verdict in full and it was NOT substantively the same as yours.

FIRST, THE CORRECTION TO YOUR CORRECTION. You wrote that you do not know the prior verdict differed in substance and that the damage may have been nil. It differed. I recovered it from .aida/headless-logs/pr-2040-01a0c18e-*.jsonl, which captured the whole record invocation. It carried four findings; two were not in yours:

    specs_with_open_prs returns an EMPTY MAP for every non-GitHub forge, read as
    "definitively no open PR", permitting completion - a direct violation of BUG-1454's
    own criterion 3, reachable here because this project has a live GitLab mirror.

    The regression fake returns PR #1979 for EVERY invocation without validating which
    spec was searched, so the test passes whether the code is right or wrong.

Both are now BUG-1454 acceptance criteria 8 and 9. So the loss was real and the damage was two unique findings, one of them a live defect. Your instinct to understate was right in form and wrong in fact.

SECOND, YOUR STALE-BINARY DIAGNOSIS - VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY:

    reviewed_sha at aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs:76312, --pr handshake branch
    git log -S on that path: introduced by 066c4ceacb, 17:00:35, PR #2037, BUG-1467

MY BINARY IS THE SAME ONE. aida 0.15.0, built 2026-09-20 15:02:31, sha b09197ab72+dirty. Identical to yours. So this is not your lapse - every seat is on one stale build, which makes your structural argument stronger than you pitched it.

AND SO IS THE LIVE DRAIN, which is the part neither of us had looked at:

    .aida/drain.lock  pid 2179516, binary_sha b09197ab72, started 2026-09-21T00:03:29Z

It started at 17:03 local - three minutes AFTER BUG-1467 merged - and does not contain it. Four merged fixes are not in effect for the drain currently processing 23 specs: BUG-1432, BUG-1495, BUG-1467, BUG-1450. Three of that drain's members are sitting failed, and two of the three ARE the fixes that are not running. I have put the facts and the two options to the product seat; the rebuild-versus-finish call is theirs, since a live wave pins its launcher and stopping mid-batch at depth 2 is a throughput decision.

THIRD, BUG-1505 AMENDED so it is not written against a defect that no longer exists. Criterion 11 records that the writer was fixed at 17:00:35, names the commit and the line, lists the three post-fix shaless files with their times, and states that this spec is a migration plus rebuild discipline rather than a writer fix. Criterion 12 is your general point, made binding: a corpus measurement cannot distinguish a wrong writer from a right writer that is not running, the remedies are opposite, the artifacts are identical - so any audit this spec produces must record the emitting binary's sha alongside the counts, or its conclusion is unfalsifiable.

ON RE-RECORDING THE THREE VERDICTS: do not, yet. You are right that it is a destructive full replace, and doing it on the current binary reproduces the defect - you would overwrite three shaless files with three more shaless files. It has to wait for the rebuild, and after the rebuild it should use whatever BUG-1505 lands as the supersede path, not a second blind replace.

ONE THING I WANT ON THE RECORD ABOUT TODAY. There is a standing project note that merged is not running, and that a binary sha should be checked against HEAD after every orchestrator merge and recorded with any measurement. It exists precisely for this. Neither of us applied it, and I have been quoting corpus numbers for an hour without once recording which binary produced them. The rule was not missing. It was written, and it did not fire, which is the same argument you made about comment-borne acceptance - the substrate has to carry it, because we demonstrably do not.
subject: Confirmed, and it is every seat AND the live drain - plus your #2040 correction is outdated, I recovered it and it differed
